title: Patch, Don't Rewrite: Post-Drift Rule Updates for LogRules-Style LLM Log Parsers

contributions.purpose: Define and motivate the problem of updating an LLM log parser's rule repository when log templates drift.
contributions.mechanism: Introduce the rule repository update problem for LogRules-style parsers and empirically contrast full rewriting against conservative patching.
contributions.evaluation: Naive Rewrite underperforms; it achieves only marginally better accuracy than leaving stale rules unchanged, and Patch beats it by +8.1 FGA points.
contributions.domain: LLM-based log parsing under template drift
contributions.source_quote: We identify the rule repository update problem for LogRules-style LLM log parsers and show that naive rewriting underperforms conservative patching.

contributions.purpose: Update a stale rule repository without losing effective pre-drift rules.
contributions.mechanism: Patch: a conservative update policy that generates a small set of delta rules targeting drifted patterns and prepends them to the unchanged original repository.
contributions.evaluation: 0.2742 overall FGA, +8.1pp over Rewrite; +14.1 points on drifted templates and +5.5 points on stable templates.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Patch, which generates targeted delta rules and prepends them to the unchanged original repository, achieving +8.1 FGA improvement over Rewrite.

contributions.purpose: Explain why prepending delta rules outperforms rewriting.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis attributing success to decoupling drift adaptation from stable-template handling (stability-plasticity).
contributions.evaluation: Patch preserves pre-drift knowledge while adding targeted capacity for new patterns, avoiding regressions on stable templates.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze why Patch succeeds: it decouples drift adaptation from stable-template handling, preserving pre-drift knowledge while adding targeted capacity for new patterns.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This approach mirrors the stability-plasticity principle from continual learning (Wang et al., 2023).

LogRules and other LLM-based approaches focus primarily on initial parsing performance and do not address how to update the parser when log templates drift over time. Our work specifically addresses this gap by proposing update policies for maintaining rule repositories under template drift.
We build upon the LogRules framework (Huang et al., 2025), which separates log parsing into two phases: induction and deduction.

notes: Positive-result method paper built on LogRules (Huang et al. 2025). Contains a negative finding about the intuitive baseline: full Rewrite is only marginally better than doing nothing (stale rules). Evaluated on a single synthetic drift benchmark.
